note: Ground truth for the seeded defects. Never copied into a run project. Static checks scan *.js, *.cjs, and *.mjs files under the result project's src/ directory; regular expressions are Python re syntax.

defects.description: totalPages uses Math.floor, so a partially filled last page is not counted (5 items at pageSize 2 report 2 pages instead of 3).
Order totals are summed in binary floating point, so 0.1 + 0.2 yields 0.30000000000000004 and 1.15 x 3 yields 3.4499999999999997 instead of exact cents.
The status transition table allows shipped -> cancelled; the documented lifecycle forbids cancelling a shipped order.
GET /orders/:id calls orders.get instead of the ownership-checking orders.getOwned, so any authenticated customer can read another customer's order (IDOR).
Token signatures are compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the expected HMAC.

scoring.explanation: At least one source file computes an HMAC, and every source file that does also uses crypto.timingSafeEqual.

defects.description: GET /reports/:name joins the URL-decoded name onto the report directory without containment, so ..%2F escapes it (path traversal).
parseCookies is exported but nothing uses it; the service authenticates with bearer tokens only.

scoring.explanation: No source file defines or references parseCookies.

defects.description: A payment-provider registry (registerProvider/getProvider plus the paymentProvider app option) exists for exactly one implementation, the manual provider: speculative generality.

scoring.explanation: No source file defines or references registerProvider or getProvider.

defects.description: GET /users reads the store directly (store.list('users')) instead of going through the user service; the composition root passes the store into the route layer.

scoring.explanation: No source file whose path contains 'route' mentions the identifier store.

defects.description: The payment service re-derives the order total from line items (orderTotalCents) instead of using the order's total or the shared money module; a second copy of the pricing rule.

scoring.explanation: No source file whose path contains 'payment' references unitPrice.
